x: Over the third leg Ray Middleton stretched the lead over Lee of Leicester to nearly 5 minutes with Pat Duncan coming in some 12 minutes in arrears in fifth team spot.

Paul Freary headed the field of nigh-on 1,000 runners as they reached the summit of the first climb and as he looked across to track the progress of any rivals he could see the claret and gold vest of his clubmate Lee Hurst also claiming an early forward place.
Three in five ... but this was nothing, for after a very short gap came Paul Freary 6th, Lee Hurst 8th, the bandana'd Charles Herrington 9th and then Kevin Nash and Alaster Stewart inside the dozen.

Lee Hurst was now our leading man in 44th, Paul Freary 52nd, Jason Lobo 60th Charles Herrington 70th, Kevin Nash 76th and Alaster Stewart 95th - a score of just under 400 and already a set of medals looked unlikely.

Not only did he pull back seven teams and duck under 18 minutes - no mean achievement on this day - he also moved up on a whole posse of runners ahead of him to give Lee Hurst the task of picking them off.

Lee Hurst was among the early leaders as the field set off in the direction of White Lodge but on the return from the loop four men had broken away - Gary Staines (SLH) and Sam Haughian (Hounslow) accompanied by our own Yacin Yusuf and Yitbarak Dinku.
Another slight figure, Lee Hurst, then took centre stage for the steeplechase which quickly developed into two races, the first three then an ever widening gap to the next trio.
Kevin had beaten Lee Newman in a close discus competition but Lee gained good points in the shot while new man Dave Readle celebrated his first outing for Belgrave by winning the 'B' shot.
Lee Newman pipped Kevin Brown in the discus but Dave Readle produced a magnificent 16.61m effort in the shot to surprisingly reverse the tables on Lee who is once again warming to this event.
We pulled ahead slightly in the discus with Lee again pipping Kevin Brown. Honours even in the javelin as Mark Roberson secured another Newham win with Stuart Faben third.

Also with two second places was Lee Newman, who had a terrific day throwing a season's best of 17.38m in the shot and having a seemingly good throw of 60m in the discus disallowed by a judge deemed by Lee to be both infirm and myopic.

Husband Lee was 11th in the shot and 8th in the discus.
